analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: MO' BOUNCE
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +58bps at 7,757 with a $400mm MOC imbalance to buy. NDX +113bps at 29,822, R2K +36bps at 2,783, Dow +69bps at 52,857. Volume was 15.887bn shares vs ytd daily average of 18.532bn.
Market was lifted by momentum and chasing in high-velocity pockets, with SPCX call options above 1m contracts.

Mag7 lagged. Bartlett attributes this to competition concerns after SPCX SI results, rotation into SPCX, Cleveland checks weighing on GOOGL, and possible source-of-funds trading ahead of expected future issuance.
Semis bounced but felt underwhelming after 10 of 11 sessions lower, despite positive news flow and constructive global tech price action overnight (SMCI +10% on positive pre-announcement).

GS desk activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale, finishing +3% better to buy on muted notional. Asset managers were about flat, with demand in Financials/REITs, industrials and energy and supply in utilities, healthcare and tech. Hedge funds were small net buyers, with demand in tech, healthcare and financials and supply in communication services.

Post-bell: META +5% on a Q3 revenue beat and Q4 guide of $73-76bn vs $73.57bn consensus, with a new class of stock coming in January 2027. TSLA +4% on Q3 deliveries, with more positive qualitative commentary than recent quarters. LRCX -7.5% despite a quarterly beat. IBM +6% on software revenue acceleration.

Derivatives desk: quiet day after VIX expiry. Index vol rose across the term structure while skew compressed. Fixed-strike vol was bid on the chase higher. Buyers of short-dated upside appeared in real size, with $18m premium spent on SPY Nov 800 calls and Dec 810 calls.

Desk views right-tail hedges as historically cheap with positioning increasingly defensive, and suggests SPY Nov 800/815 call spreads offering 8x payout. S&P implied move for the rest of the week is 78bps.

Hedge funds have heavily net sold global equities in October, with short sales outpacing long buys about 5 to 1. Long leverage is in the 73rd percentile vs the past year (94th over 5 years). Short leverage is near 5-year highs (99th percentile).

market_movers.rationale: Stock +5% post-bell on a solid Q3 revenue beat and Q4 revenue guide of $73-76bn vs $73.57bn consensus. A new class of stock is coming in January 2027.
Stock +4% post-bell. Q3 deliveries were a clear beat but were already known from early October. Qualitative commentary is more positive than in recent quarters.
Stock -7.5% post-bell despite a quarterly beat. F2Q gross margin guide of 52.4% vs consensus of about 52%, and guidance slightly above the Street.
Stock +6% post-bell, up from +4% into the print. Software revenue accelerated to +9% y/y constant currency from +5% last quarter, with a rebound in Transaction Processing revenue.
